answers.text: For the driver messages, I'd say: always three lines in the same order — drop-off time, then pallet count, then any damage noted. Keep it consistent every time, that's what makes it come out the same.
Tell them: list time, customer, topic, outcome for each call, and count up how many have 'needs follow-up' as the outcome — that count goes at the top of the list.
Reading this again, access from 8am on the 22nd, six hours of work, but it says finishing on the 23rd. That doesn't sit right with me. I'd want that checked before it's filed.
118 against 96 isn't a 20% rise, that's closer to 23%. The 92% on-time figure looks right to me though, matches up. I'd get that growth number checked.
I'd sign off Output 2, it shows the actual counts, 827 out of 940, so you can see how the 88% comes about. Output 1 just states the percentage with nothing behind it.
I'd send Email 2, it has the actual volume numbers in it, stronger case.

1. Vendor pricing — yes, that's fine for a quote summary. 2. Total spend — yes. 3. Unsigned budget draft — no, not settled yet. 4. Datasheet on their website — not sure, might be alright since it's out there already. 5. Employee's home address — no, that's personal.

The hourly rates and retainer cap, I wouldn't paste those in as they are, feels too sensitive without a cleared tool. Same caution with the NDA part since it names both sides. The rest of it I'm less sure about.
Before the stock summary goes out, I check the totals against the warehouse system count. I do that every month before sending it on.
Step 1 is where the risk starts, since if the invoice gets read wrong there, that mistake carries all the way through.
